SECTION 4 — ESCAPE OF WATER

4.1 We will cover loss of or damage to the contents caused by water escaping from any fixed water or heating installation, or from any domestic appliance connected to such an installation.

4.2 We will not cover:
(a) damage occurring where the premises have been unoccupied for more than 30 consecutive days, unless the water supply has been turned off at the main and the system drained;
(b) the cost of repairing or replacing the installation or appliance from which the water escaped;
(c) damage caused by water entering the premises from outside the building;
(d) any amount in respect of wear, tear or gradual deterioration.

SECTION 9 — YOUR OBLIGATIONS

9.3 You must notify us as soon as reasonably possible, and in any event within 30 days, of any event which may give rise to a claim. Failure to do so may prejudice your claim to the extent that our position has been adversely affected.

9.7 Where we replace an item with a new equivalent and the replacement represents a material improvement on the item lost or damaged, we may make a proportionate deduction to reflect that improvement.

SECTION 12 — RECOVERY FROM THIRD PARTIES

12.1 We are entitled to pursue recovery in your name against any party responsible for the loss. You must provide all reasonable assistance and must not, without our written consent, admit liability or make any agreement with such a party that prejudices our right of recovery.
input.mySituation: My flat was flooded by the upstairs neighbour's washing machine three weeks ago. I am trying to work out what my own contents policy actually covers before I ring them.
input.concerns: Whether 'escape of water' covers someone else's appliance, whether the three weeks has already cost me the claim, and what 'betterment' means when they replace a ten-year-old carpet.

document.type: Home contents insurance policy — Section extracts covering escape of water, policyholder obligations, betterment, and third-party recovery
document.bottom_line: The escape of water cover in Section 4.1 covers water escaping from a domestic appliance connected to a fixed water or heating installation. Whether your neighbour's washing machine qualifies depends on whether it was connected to the building's fixed water supply — you should confirm this with the insurer when you notify them. You are within the 30-day notification deadline if you contact them now. A proportionate deduction may be applied when replacing a ten-year-old carpet, and a separate deduction may also apply for wear and tear.

needs_attention.what: Notify your insurer of the flood event
needs_attention.why_it_matters_to_you: The flood happened three weeks ago; the document requires notification within 30 days
needs_attention.deadline: Within 30 days of the event. If the flood was exactly 21 days ago, approximately 9 days remain — but if your date is approximate, treat this as urgent
needs_attention.if_you_do_nothing: The document states that failure to notify within 30 days may prejudice your claim to the extent the insurer's position has been adversely affected
needs_attention.what_to_do: Notify the insurer now, before you complete all your preparation, so the deadline is met

needs_attention.what: Do not admit liability to the neighbour or make any agreement with them about the loss without the insurer's written consent
needs_attention.why_it_matters_to_you: The neighbour's washing machine caused the damage; the insurer may wish to pursue recovery from them under Section 12.1
needs_attention.if_you_do_nothing: An agreement or admission made without written consent could prejudice the insurer's right of recovery, which Section 12.1 expressly prohibits
needs_attention.what_to_do: Avoid settling informally with the neighbour or signing anything until the insurer has confirmed in writing that it consents

needs_attention.what: Provide all reasonable assistance to the insurer if it pursues recovery from the neighbour
needs_attention.why_it_matters_to_you: The neighbour is the responsible third party; Section 12.1 gives the insurer the right to pursue recovery in your name
needs_attention.what_to_do: Keep records of communications with the neighbour, any acknowledgements they made, and anything the building management said — these may be needed

money.what: Betterment deduction on the carpet replacement
money.amount_or_rule: If the replacement carpet is a material improvement on the damaged one, the insurer may make a proportionate deduction to reflect that improvement. The document gives the insurer discretion on the amount; no formula or cap is stated.
money.when: At the point of settlement or replacement

money.what: No cover for the cost of repairing or replacing the neighbour's washing machine itself
money.amount_or_rule: The cost of the appliance from which water escaped is excluded entirely — this is a zero-benefit item under your contents policy

money.what: No cover for any portion of the carpet loss attributed to wear, tear or gradual deterioration
money.amount_or_rule: Any amount representing wear and tear is excluded. For a ten-year-old carpet, the insurer may attribute some portion of the value to deterioration rather than flood damage. The document does not state a formula.

also_relevant.what: The escape of water cover in Section 4.1 extends to water escaping from a domestic appliance connected to a fixed installation — which a washing machine plumbed into the building's water supply would be
also_relevant.why_it_matters: Your concern was whether the neighbour's appliance qualifies. Section 4.1 does not restrict cover to appliances within your own flat; it covers damage to your contents caused by water escaping from any such appliance. Whether the neighbour's machine was connected to a fixed installation is a factual question about that machine, not a policy restriction.

also_relevant.what: Whether the water entered your flat from outside the building or through the building's internal structure matters to cover
also_relevant.why_it_matters: Section 4.2(c) excludes damage caused by water entering from outside the building. Water coming through a ceiling from an upstairs flat is internal to the building, which would not trigger this exclusion — unless the path of the water involved an external element such as an outside drain or exterior wall breach.

also_relevant.what: The 'prejudice' language in the notification clause limits but does not automatically void a late or borderline-late claim
also_relevant.why_it_matters: Section 9.3 says failure to notify may prejudice your claim to the extent the insurer's position has been adversely affected — not that the claim is automatically refused. If you notify promptly now and the insurer cannot point to actual adverse effect from the three-week gap, this clause may not reduce your recovery. The document does not resolve how the insurer will apply it.

doesnt_appear_relevant.why: You described the flood as affecting your flat, implying you occupy it. An unoccupied-premises exclusion requires more than 30 consecutive days of unoccupancy.
doesnt_appear_relevant.could_change_if: You have been away from the flat for more than 30 consecutive days, or you do not live there full-time

doesnt_appear_relevant.what: Water entering from outside the building (Section 4.2(c))
doesnt_appear_relevant.why: The source of the water was the upstairs neighbour's washing machine — an internal source. Water travelling through the floor/ceiling of the building is not the same as water entering from outside.
doesnt_appear_relevant.could_change_if: The water's path involved an external element, such as an outside drain or exterior wall breach

buried_but_important.what: The 'prejudice' qualifier on late notification is conditional, not an automatic bar — but the document leaves its application entirely to the insurer's assessment
buried_but_important.why_easy_to_miss: The word 'may' and the limiting phrase 'to the extent that our position has been adversely affected' in Section 9.3 mean the insurer cannot refuse your claim simply because you notified late; the refusal or reduction depends on showing actual adverse effect from the delay.

buried_but_important.what: The betterment deduction in Section 9.7 applies only when replacement represents a 'material improvement' — it is not automatic on any new-for-old replacement
buried_but_important.why_easy_to_miss: The betterment deduction in Section 9.7 applies only when the replacement represents a 'material improvement' — it is not automatic on any new-for-old replacement. The word 'material' sets a threshold the insurer must meet before making the deduction.

buried_but_important.what: Section 4.2(d) excludes wear, tear and gradual deterioration as a separate head of exclusion from betterment — a claim could face both reductions applied independently
buried_but_important.why_easy_to_miss: Betterment (Section 9.7) and the wear-and-tear exclusion (Section 4.2(d)) appear in different sections. Both could apply to a replacement carpet: the insurer may deduct for material improvement and also deduct any portion attributable to wear and tear as a separate exclusion.

practical_next_steps: Notify the insurer today or within the next day or two — you can flag that you are still gathering details, but getting the notification in now protects you against the 30-day limit
Photograph or video all damaged contents and the carpet before cleaning, moving or disposal — the insurer may need this evidence to assess the claim.
Write down — or save — any messages or statements from the upstairs neighbour acknowledging the washing machine leak
Do not agree to any payment or settlement with the neighbour, or sign anything they offer, without first getting written consent from your insurer
When you call, ask the insurer to confirm in writing how it will apply Section 9.3 given the three-week gap, so you have a record of their position
questions_to_ask: Given that I am notifying you three weeks after the event, will you confirm in writing whether you consider your position to have been adversely affected, and if so, in what way?
The water came from my neighbour's washing machine upstairs — can you confirm this falls within 'any domestic appliance connected to a fixed water or heating installation' under Section 4.1?
For the carpet replacement, how will you assess whether the replacement represents a 'material improvement,' and will you also apply a separate wear-and-tear reduction under Section 4.2(d)?
Do you intend to pursue recovery from my upstairs neighbour under Section 12.1, and if so, what do you need from me to support that?
Is there anything I should not say or agree to with the neighbour or the building management while the claim is open?

outside_help.question: Whether the betterment deduction and the wear-and-tear exclusion can both be applied to the same carpet, and whether that is consistent with the policy wording
outside_help.why_the_document_doesnt_resolve_it: The document does not state whether betterment and wear-and-tear reductions are applied to the same item independently or as a single combined reduction, or what the calculation looks like in practice. The insurer has discretion to make a 'proportionate deduction' for betterment under Section 9.7, but the document leaves the method to their assessment.
outside_help.who_to_ask_first: Your insurer — ask them to explain in writing how both sections will be applied before any settlement figure is agreed

MIETVERTRAG — ÄNDERUNGSMITTEILUNG (Wirkung ab 1. September 2026)
Sehr geehrte Mieterin, sehr geehrter Mieter,
1. Die monatliche Kaltmiete erhöht sich um 85 EUR aufgrund der ortsüblichen Vergleichsmiete. Widerspruch bis 15. August 2026 schriftlich.
2. Nebenkostenvorauszahlung steigt um 40 EUR pro Monat. Die Jahresabrechnung ergab eine Nachzahlung von 320 EUR, fällig binnen 30 Tagen.
3. Neue Hausordnung: Ruhezeiten 22-7 Uhr, Waschküche nur mit Buchung über das neue Online-Portal (Registrierung erforderlich).
4. Haustierhaltung: Hunde nur mit schriftlicher Genehmigung; bestehende Genehmigungen bleiben gültig.
5. Für Fragen zur Mieterhöhung empfehlen wir rechtliche Beratung durch den Mieterverein.
6. Kündigungsfrist unverändert 3 Monate.
input.mySituation: Alleinstehend, 34, mit Hund, arbeite im Homeoffice, knappes Budget
input.concerns: Ob ich der Mieterhöhung widersprechen kann

document.bottom_line: Die Widerspruchsfrist gegen die Mieterhöhung (15. August 2026) ist bereits abgelaufen – das ist die dringlichste Information für Sie, da sie Ihr knappes Budget direkt betrifft.

needs_attention.what: Nachzahlung aus der Nebenkostenabrechnung von 320 EUR bezahlen
needs_attention.why_it_matters_to_you: Sie haben ein knappes Budget – diese Zahlung ist fällig und nicht optional.
needs_attention.deadline: Binnen 30 Tagen ab Datum des Schreibens – das genaue Datum des Schreibens ist nicht angegeben, daher lässt sich die Frist nicht exakt berechnen.
needs_attention.if_you_do_nothing: Das Dokument nennt keine Konsequenz, aber die Fälligkeit ist ausdrücklich gesetzt.
needs_attention.what_to_do: Den Betrag von 320 EUR innerhalb der 30-Tage-Frist überweisen. Das genaue Fälligkeitsdatum beim Vermieter erfragen, falls das Schreibdatum unklar ist.

needs_attention.what: Für die Waschküche im neuen Online-Portal registrieren, um sie weiter nutzen zu können
needs_attention.why_it_matters_to_you: Sie können die Waschküche ohne Registrierung nicht buchen, laut Dokument.
needs_attention.if_you_do_nothing: Das Dokument nennt keine explizite Konsequenz, aber die Buchung über das Portal wird als Voraussetzung für die Nutzung bezeichnet.

needs_attention.what: Schriftliche Genehmigung für Ihren Hund prüfen und sicherstellen, dass sie vorliegt
needs_attention.why_it_matters_to_you: Sie haben einen Hund – das Dokument verlangt eine schriftliche Genehmigung. Bestehende Genehmigungen bleiben laut Dokument gültig, aber nur wenn sie tatsächlich existieren.
needs_attention.if_you_do_nothing: Das Dokument nennt keine Konsequenz für fehlende Genehmigung, regelt aber Hunde ausdrücklich als genehmigungspflichtig.
needs_attention.what_to_do: Prüfen, ob eine schriftliche Genehmigung in Ihren Unterlagen vorhanden ist. Falls nicht, beim Vermieter nachfragen.

money.when: Innerhalb von 30 Tagen ab Datum des Schreibens

money.amount_or_rule: +125 EUR pro Monat (85 EUR Kaltmiete + 40 EUR Nebenkosten), zusätzlich zur einmaligen Nachzahlung von 320 EUR

also_relevant.what: Der Widerspruch gegen die Mieterhöhung war bis 15. August 2026 möglich – diese Frist ist heute (4. September 2026) abgelaufen.
also_relevant.why_it_matters: Sie fragen, ob Sie widersprechen können. Laut Dokument war die Frist der 15. August 2026; dieser Termin liegt in der Vergangenheit.

also_relevant.what: Der Vermieter empfiehlt selbst rechtliche Beratung durch den Mieterverein bei Fragen zur Mieterhöhung.
also_relevant.why_it_matters: Bei knappem Budget und Unsicherheit über die Mieterhöhung ist dies ein im Dokument genannter Anlaufpunkt – Mietervereine bieten in Deutschland oft günstige oder kostenlose Erstberatung.

also_relevant.what: Ruhezeiten 22 bis 7 Uhr gemäß neuer Hausordnung
also_relevant.why_it_matters: Mit Hund und Homeoffice (unregelmäßige Arbeitszeiten möglich) ist die Kenntnis der Ruhezeiten relevant.

doesnt_appear_relevant.why: Sie haben nicht geäußert, dass Sie kündigen möchten oder eine Kündigung in Betracht ziehen.
doesnt_appear_relevant.could_change_if: Sie erwägen, wegen der Mieterhöhung oder aus anderen Gründen auszuziehen.

buried_but_important.what: Die Widerspruchsfrist steht im gleichen Satz wie die Ankündigung der Mieterhöhung und wird nicht gesondert hervorgehoben – sie lautet 15. August 2026, was heute bereits überschritten ist.
buried_but_important.why_easy_to_miss: Frist und Begründung der Mieterhöhung stehen in einer einzigen kurzen Ziffer; es gibt keine separate Fristenübersicht im Dokument.

buried_but_important.what: Bestehende Hundehalter-Genehmigungen bleiben laut Dokument gültig – aber nur solche, die tatsächlich schriftlich erteilt wurden.
buried_but_important.why_easy_to_miss: Der Satz 'bestehende Genehmigungen bleiben gültig' bezieht sich auf Genehmigungen, die bereits schriftlich erteilt wurden. Das Dokument macht nicht deutlich, dass Sie nachweisen müssen, dass eine solche Genehmigung tatsächlich vorliegt.

practical_next_steps: Kontaktieren Sie Ihren Mieterverein, um zu klären, ob die Mieterhöhung formell zulässig ist oder ob Einwände noch möglich sind – trotz abgelaufener Frist können formale Fehler relevant sein.

Suchen Sie Ihren Mieterverein auf: Das Dokument empfiehlt dies ausdrücklich, und Mietervereine können prüfen, ob trotz abgelaufener Frist rechtliche Handlungsoptionen bestehen – etwa wenn die Mieterhöhung formell fehlerhaft ist.
Legen Sie die 320-EUR-Nachzahlung termingerecht zurück, auch wenn Sie gleichzeitig rechtliche Beratung einholen.
Suchen Sie die schriftliche Hundehalter-Genehmigung aus Ihren Unterlagen heraus und bewahren Sie sie griffbereit auf.
Registrieren Sie sich im Online-Portal für die Waschküche, sobald der Zugang verfügbar ist.
questions_to_ask: Wann genau wurde dieses Schreiben ausgestellt oder zugestellt? (Für die 30-Tage-Frist der Nebenkostennachzahlung relevant.)
Liegt eine schriftliche Genehmigung zur Hundehaltung in meiner Akte vor, und kann ich eine Kopie erhalten?
Wie und wann kann ich mich für das Online-Portal der Waschküche registrieren?
Auf welchem Mietspiegel oder welcher Vergleichsmiete basiert die Erhöhung um 85 EUR?

outside_help.question: Kann die Mieterhöhung noch angefochten werden, obwohl die im Dokument genannte Widerspruchsfrist abgelaufen ist – etwa wegen formeller Fehler?
outside_help.why_the_document_doesnt_resolve_it: Das Dokument nennt nur die Frist und empfiehlt Beratung, regelt aber nicht, welche Rechte bei Fristversäumnis oder formellen Mängeln bestehen.
outside_help.who_to_ask_first: Mieterverein (im Dokument selbst empfohlen, Ziffer 5) – vor einem Rechtsanwalt.
